claims.text: The untreated high-entropy alloy contains no lubricating secondary phase.
The intervention is bulk incorporation of 2–5 vol% h-BN nanoplatelets into the high-entropy alloy by powder metallurgy.
Bulk-incorporated h-BN nanoplatelets will produce an in situ lubricious tribolayer during sliding.
h-BN nanoplatelets have a layered structure relevant to their function as the structural mediator.
Mechanical shear during sliding will orient the h-BN nanoplatelets at the contact interface.
The oriented h-BN nanoplatelets will form a continuous tribolayer at the contact interface.
The resulting h-BN-containing tribolayer will have low shear strength.
The low-shear-strength tribolayer will reduce interfacial friction.
The tribolayer will protect the alloy from severe wear.
The h-BN-modified alloy will have a friction coefficient approximately 30–40% lower than that of the untreated alloy under similar conditions.
The h-BN-modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than the untreated alloy.
The reductions in friction and wear will be sustained from ambient temperature to approximately 500 °C in ambient atmosphere under controlled sliding loads.
Performance may differ under extreme loads, high-velocity impacts, or non-ambient atmospheres.
Long-term stability of the h-BN dispersion in the alloy matrix is uncertain.
The exact magnitude of improvement across all service conditions and the scalability of manufacturing are uncertain.
